counter_evidence.description: The revision is written before journal removal, creating the asserted post-commit crash window.
Recovery checks integrity and supersession but never compares base_revision with the current revision before rollback.
Superseded journals are refused, but a journal left by a successful commit is not marked superseded.

challenges.reasoning_summary: Falsification failed. Locking, integrity verification, per-write fencing, and superseded-journal handling do not distinguish an interrupted pre-commit journal from the genuine journal left after the revision reached R+1. The source and Opus runtime evidence establish silent rollback to healthy R.

counter_evidence.description: The digest accurately describes the reduced route after headers and provider-specific behavior have been omitted.
extraHeaders and costExtractor are explicitly undefined and providerKind is forced to openai-compatible.
Named-provider factories support headers, provider identity, and OpenRouter cost extraction, confirming that the paid kernel drops supported configuration.

counter_evidence.requirement_ref: Closure Contract 3 acceptance criterion covering route-critical headers and named routes
counter_evidence.description: Configured route-critical headers are expressly within the required resolved-operation identity.

challenges.reasoning_summary: The factual configuration-fidelity defect stands. Digest and transport agree only because both omit the configured fields; this prevents post-resolution drift but does not honor the named profile. MEDIUM is appropriate because impact is confined to header-dependent profiles and commonly causes failed or degraded calls rather than silent trusted-state corruption.

counter_evidence.description: The current production provider merges windows in a Map keyed by source file and emits at most one slice per path.
The deduplication key omits rendered text and multiplicity, and a later duplicate's text is discarded.
The committed test treats same-window deduplication as intended but does not test differing text under the same key.

challenges.reasoning_summary: The kernel weakness is real, while the stated production-reachability limitation is also supported. The normal provider prevents this exact differing-text duplicate today, so LOW remains appropriate. A distinct late finding addresses ordinary model-visible context omitted from bundle identity.

counter_evidence.description: The raw content digests are named fields inside a versioned LCO:STRUCTURE binding digest.
The digests are compared in fixed semantic positions, preventing a demonstrated current cross-field substitution.
Manifest, graph, and source-set digests are returned as StructuralIdentity and drive freshness, so they are trust-bearing under the contract.

challenges.reasoning_summary: The enclosing binding contains the practical confusion risk but does not falsify the ownership observation: three load-bearing structural identities are locally hashed outside canonical.ts. With no current misacceptance demonstrated, LOW is correctly calibrated.

counter_evidence.description: The second LCO:PAID_CONTEXT value is persisted as analysis input lineage.
The persisted context_digest is only shape-validated as a SHA-256 string.
Production source contains only the construction site and schema field; no verifier or authority decision accepts context_digest.
Citation authority recomputes the sealed-record payload and never accepts the persisted raw-bundle digest in its place.

challenges.reasoning_summary: Reuse of the domain/version is factual, but the second value has no current authority-bearing verification site. The surviving issue is schema naming and future-proofing, not present domain confusion or trusted-effect acceptance.

severity_recalibration.justification: The second digest is audit lineage rather than a currently verified authority identity, so no present requirement-breaching effect was demonstrated.

counter_evidence.description: The renewal graph-reader/provider edge is type-only and erased at runtime.
The eval component includes a genuine value import, supporting the distinction between type-only and runtime SCCs.

counter_evidence.command_ref: Independent Codex in-memory Tarjan scan over 146 production TypeScript modules
counter_evidence.description: The independent scan also found four total SCCs and no focus cycle involving trust, core records, project, snapshot, planner, or recovery.

challenges.reasoning_summary: The observation is accurate and correctly classified as non-defective for Contract 6. Independent cycle analysis corroborated the absence of a trust-ownership SCC.

late_findings.title: Sealed bundle identity omits ordinary model-visible node, edge, and fact bytes
late_findings.claim: Production prompt context contains slices, nodes, edges, and structural facts, but sealContextBundle receives only file slices. Consequently bundle_id does not identify the complete rendered context supplied to the model, and the separate full-bundle context_digest is not joined to bundle_id or consent before transport.

evidence.description: The production bundle contains ordered slices, nodes, edges, and derived facts.
Only file_slice items are passed to sealContextBundle.
The sealed digest contains slice-record facts but no node, edge, fact, scope, truncation, warning, or final-rendering fields.
All ContextBundle item classes are projected and serialized into the model-visible prompt.
The full-bundle digest is persisted, but req.bundle and deps.context are accepted separately without an equality join.

evidence.requirement_ref: Evidence acceptance criteria requiring identity over exact rendered model-visible context
evidence.description: The authoritative requirement covers the complete serialized context rather than only citable slices.

counter_evidence.description: Retained slices are text-hashed and joined to project, snapshot, manifest, and graph digests.
The graph digest indirectly constrains node and edge source bytes under the current deterministic provider, reducing but not eliminating the direct identity gap.

late_findings.reasoning_summary: Opus confined its evidence concern to an unreachable duplicate-window variant and missed that complete normal prompts include model-visible item classes excluded from sealed identity.
late_findings.failure_scenario: Two analyses retain the same file slices and structural digests but differ in context selection, ordering, limits, node/fact projection, or through a post-seal req.bundle substitution. The sealed bundle ID remains unchanged while the model receives different context bytes.
late_findings.impact: Citation lineage cannot directly prove which complete context the model saw, matching the contract's release-blocking context-substitution class.
late_findings.root_cause: Citation sealing and prompt serialization use different context projections with no enforced canonical join.
late_findings.verification_method: Source reconstruction and an independent in-memory prompt-versus-bundle identity comparison.
late_findings.residual_uncertainty: Current graph digests and deterministic defaults indirectly constrain much of the omitted context; arbitrary substitution exploitability depends on API reachability.

late_findings.title: Planner fingerprint bypasses canonical digest ownership and its guard
late_findings.category: Closure Contracts 5 and 6 — Consumer Mediation / Canonical Ownership
late_findings.claim: Renewal planning persists manifest.council_run.config_fingerprint using sha256Content(JSON.stringify(...)) rather than a versioned domainDigest. The architecture guard intended to reject this idiom checks one line at a time and misses the current multiline call.

evidence.description: The persisted configuration fingerprint is an undomained JSON hash.

evidence.symbol: no ad-hoc trust-bearing digest idioms outside the canonical layer
evidence.description: The guard requires hash construction and JSON.stringify to occur on the same physical line; production splits them across lines 432-433.

evidence.requirement_ref: Closure Contract 6 requires zero trust-bearing ad-hoc digests
evidence.description: Planner/export load-bearing truth is expressly within the audit census.

counter_evidence.description: The current payload is fixed and deterministic and does not directly authorize a state mutation.

late_findings.reasoning_summary: Opus identified structural raw digests but missed the planner fingerprint because the repository guard has the same formatting-sensitive blind spot.
late_findings.failure_scenario: A verifier or exporter treats config_fingerprint as canonical run identity, but it has no domain/version discriminator and can drift outside canonical ownership while the architecture test remains green.
late_findings.impact: The zero ad-hoc trust-digest claim is inaccurate. No present authority escalation was demonstrated, limiting severity to Medium.
late_findings.root_cause: A line-oriented lexical guard replaced semantic call-expression analysis, and the planner retained a raw digest idiom.
late_findings.verification_method: Direct inspection of the production call and its guard.
late_findings.residual_uncertainty: If config_fingerprint is adjudicated as provenance-only rather than trust-bearing, severity should be reduced.

late_findings.title: Snapshot creation can compose structural fields from different read epochs
late_findings.claim: cmdRenewInit obtains graph counts, manifest identity, graph digest, binding digest, and Graphify version through separate reads. Its structuralIdentity call omits bindingText, and the separately parsed binding is not joined to those later bytes before snapshot construction. A concurrent rebuild can therefore commit a hybrid snapshot; staleness checks do not compare node_count, edge_count, or graphify_version.

evidence.description: Snapshot fields are sourced from multiple independently timed reads and provider calls.
Artifact-to-binding checks execute only when bindingText is supplied; init omits it.
Freshness compares file and digest fields but not the stored graph counts or Graphify version.

evidence.requirement_ref: Closure Contract 4 mixed-epoch and mid-call structural mutation criteria
evidence.description: Snapshot, manifest, graph, and binding must form one accepted epoch.

counter_evidence.description: Each individual provider.graph call verifies a bound artifact triple.
Repeated builds of unchanged sources commonly yield equal counts, and paid-result promotion later rechecks the current triple.

late_findings.reasoning_summary: Stable A/B artifact probes do not exercise mutation between the multiple reads used to assemble the snapshot.
late_findings.failure_scenario: Refresh A reads graph counts from epoch A. Refresh B completes before A's later reads. A records manifest, graph, and binding from B with counts from A; freshness can still report healthy because it never compares those counts.
late_findings.impact: The snapshot identity can describe an epoch that never existed. Current use of the differing fields is limited, supporting Medium severity.
late_findings.root_cause: Snapshot construction does not consume one immutable verified structural result containing every stored field.
late_findings.residual_uncertainty: Runtime confirmation remains necessary because the trigger requires concurrent valid builds with differing counts or versions.

late_findings.title: Persistent abort-evidence write failure leaves no durable fail-closed marker
late_findings.claim: writeAbortEvidence catches and discards all three write failures. In a foreign-journal abort, the concurrent owner can later remove its journal, leaving future readers with neither journal nor sidecar even though zombie bytes may have landed.

evidence.description: These paths rely on the sidecar as durable evidence surviving another writer's journal cleanup.
After the third failed write the function returns without a durable marker or failed-persistence result.

evidence.requirement_ref: Residual R3 and Closure Contract 1 zombie-writer criterion
evidence.description: A later transaction must not erase the only evidence needed to keep possible zombie bytes untrusted.

counter_evidence.description: Transient failures receive three attempts, and the current caller still receives recovery_required.
Persistent path-selective failure while other trusted writes succeed is uncommon, so severity is capped at Medium.

requirement_refs: Closure Contract 1 zombie and ownership fencing
late_findings.reasoning_summary: Opus showed that a successfully written sidecar fails closed but did not address the terminal all-retries-failed branch, which leaves only a process-local exception.
late_findings.failure_scenario: Writer A may have landed a zombie write while B owns the journal. All sidecar attempts fail; A exits. B completes and removes its journal. A late write lands, and a new process sees no marker.
late_findings.impact: Possible silent torn state under a constrained double-failure schedule.
late_findings.root_cause: The durable evidence channel is best-effort, and its terminal failure is not represented persistently.
late_findings.residual_uncertainty: Whether this persistent path-selective filesystem failure belongs to the supported local failure model requires targeted adjudication.
